Legacy identity: `FOS-000016`. Original source: [immutable historical definition](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/73f891d6c0cf498ac92e804d7d0f0cd344a083f5/local-docs/reviews/observability-sweep.md).

Shared requirements and grouping: https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/8. All original criteria below remain required. Source status statements below describe their historical revision; current delivery evidence is recorded separately. Original relative links are resolved below.

## Original definition (verbatim)

16. **FOS-000016 — Add database finalization that can report failure.** **M, one backend at a time; depends on `FOS-000003` and `FOS-000009`; §1, §6.** [DatabaseInterface:149](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/fossilize_db.hpp#L149) exposes void flush; [StreamArchive:1072](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/fossilize_db.cpp#L1072) ignores flush/close failures; [ZIP:776](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/556da9ff7d7616704dda515756219ab1dab693ec/fossilize_db.cpp#L776) only logs finalization failures during destruction. Provide explicit checked finalization before nonthrowing destruction and sticky I/O status with underlying error. Start with stream archives (E4), then directory/ZIP/concurrent wrappers. Preserve valid prefixes and define behavior after a partial entry write; do not blindly retry into a damaged tail. **Check:** buffered ENOSPC, partial write, ZIP finalize failure, child-backend failure, repeated finalize. Audit public virtual-interface compatibility: use a deliberate additive/versioned migration rather than casually breaking external implementations. Promise flush/close completion unless stronger durability is explicitly implemented.

   **Required automated success criteria — pending implementation:**

   - **Database-backend fault matrix:** For every migrated stream, directory, ZIP and concurrent backend, inject write, flush, close/finalize and delegated child errors. Explicit finalization returns a sticky originating failure before destruction; E4 returns nonzero after the CLI adopts the checked result.
   - **Recovery and ownership tests:** Repeated finalization follows the documented idempotence contract; destruction does not throw or double-close. After a partial entry failure, intact prior entries remain readable and later calls follow the documented stopped/recovery behavior rather than appending blindly to a damaged tail.
   - **Interface compatibility fixtures:** Compile/link an old-style external DatabaseInterface implementation against every API version claimed source-compatible. If binary compatibility is claimed, also run a prebuilt compatible consumer fixture; otherwise test explicit version rejection and document the break.
